The source spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the matter. It was not clear if Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé would meet directly with Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele. The visit comes as Bukele has ramped up his offensive against Haiti’s gangs with at least 2,500 Salvadoran forces now operating in Haiti. The offensive began in October after four Salvadoran aviation technicians went missing in an attack by gangs. Since, Bukele has sought to project an image as a crusader on crime coming to vanquish Haitian gangs, which control whole parts of Haiti’s territory and are deeply entwined with some of the country’s political elite. On Sunday, Haitian police and Salvadoran soldiers destroyed a home of Wilson Joseph, the leader of 400 Mawozo, one of Haiti’s most powerful gangs. The operation was first reported by Haitian media and confirmed by Damian Merlo, a lobbyist working for El Salvador’s government. The offensive did not kill the leader, better known as Lanmò San Jou, and Haitian gang leaders regularly cycle between a number of houses. Last Friday, two days before the operation, Bukele posted on the social media platform X asking for the location of Joseph’s house in Haitian Creole. “Give us the exact address, and we’ll destroy it,” he wrote.
